\begin{defn}[Reflexivity]
A relation $R \subseteq A^2$ is \emph{reflexive} iff, for every $x \in
A$, $Rxx$.
\end{defn}

\begin{defn}[Anti-symmetry]
A relation~$R \subseteq A^2$ is \emph{anti-sym\-met\-ric} iff, whenever both
$Rxy$ and $Ryx$, then $x=y$ (or, in other words: if $x\neq y$ then
either $\lnot Rxy$ or $\lnot Ryx$).
\end{defn}

\begin{defn}[Irreflexivity]
A relation $R \subseteq A^2$ is called \emph{irreflexive} if, for all $x \in
A$, not $Rxx$. 
\end{defn}

\begin{defn}[Asymmetry]
A relation $R \subseteq A^2$ is called \emph{asymmetric} if for no pair $x,y\in
A$ we have both $Rxy$ and~$Ryx$. 
\end{defn}

Note that if $A \neq \emptyset$, then no irreflexive relation on~$A$
is reflexive and every asymmetric relation on~$A$ is also
anti-symmetric. However, there are $R \subseteq A^2$ that are not
reflexive and also not irreflexive, and there are anti-symmetric
relations that are not asymmetric.

\textbf{تنبيه توضيحي على الأصل.} عند تثبيت المجموعة $A$، فإن وجود علاقة
عليها لا تتصف بالانعكاسية ولا باللاانعكاسية يكافئ احتواءها على عنصرين

مضادّة للتناظر لا تتصف باللاتناظرية فيكفي له أن تكون $A$ غير خالية.
% OLP0014-DOMAIN-SIZE-20260909 END

لاحظ أنه إذا كان $A \neq \emptyset$، فلا توجد علاقة لا انعكاسية على~$A$

توجد علاقات $R \subseteq A^2$ لا تتصف بالانعكاسية ولا باللاانعكاسية، كما
توجد علاقات مضادّة للتناظر لا تتصف باللاتناظرية.

mathematical_analysis.source_reading: The original existential sentence is true when it ranges over suitable domains. Read as about each previously fixed nonempty A, its first existence example additionally needs two distinct elements. The note makes that parameter explicit and does not label the original statement unconditionally false.
mathematical_analysis.editorial_english_proposition: For a fixed set A, a relation on A that is neither reflexive nor irreflexive exists if and only if A has at least two distinct elements. For the separate existence of an anti-symmetric but not asymmetric relation, nonemptiness of A suffices.

first_claim.necessity: If R is not irreflexive, some a in A satisfies Raa. If R is not reflexive, some b in A satisfies not Rbb. These witnesses must differ, since otherwise Raa and not Raa would both hold. Hence A has at least two elements.
first_claim.sufficiency: If a,b are distinct elements of A, choose R={(a,a)} as a subset of A^2. It is not irreflexive since Raa, and not reflexive since not Rbb. This works equally for finite and infinite A.
first_claim.empty_case: The only relation on the empty set is empty and satisfies both universal properties vacuously, so it is not neither.
first_claim.singleton_case: The only relations are empty (irreflexive) and the diagonal singleton (reflexive); neither is a neither-example.

second_claim.necessity: If R is anti-symmetric but not asymmetric, there exist x,y with Rxy and Ryx; anti-symmetry gives x=y. In particular A contains an element.
second_claim.sufficiency: For any a in nonempty A, R={(a,a)} is anti-symmetric, since any two-way related pair has equal entries, but not asymmetric, because Raa holds in both directions.
second_claim.empty_case: The empty relation on the empty set is asymmetric as well as anti-symmetric. Thus no such example exists there.
second_claim.singleton_case: The diagonal singleton already gives the example. Do not import the first claim's two-element requirement into this second claim.

mathematical_analysis.finite_check_scope: All 531 relations on labelled domains of sizes 0,1,2,3 are enumerated by the focused test (1+2+16+512). This confirms edge cases but does not replace the general necessity/sufficiency proofs.

terminology_decisions.source_proposition: For a fixed set A, a relation on A that is neither reflexive nor irreflexive exists if and only if A has at least two distinct elements. For the separate existence of an anti-symmetric but not asymmetric relation, nonemptiness of A suffices.
terminology_decisions.source_proposition_status: new editorial inference from cited original definitions, not a verbatim upstream sentence
